fixes.explanation: No armies in this report, baker. The report never mentions them. The leaders say the Israelites “…have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and their sons…” (Ezra 9:2). Marriage is the way they say it happened.

False is right, baker. The report says “…the leaders and officials have taken the lead in this unfaithfulness!” (Ezra 9:2). They weren't standing back. They were out front. I think that's a heavy thing to hear.

Artaxerxes, king of Persia (Ezra 7:1), isn't named in this gathering, baker. Ezra says the ones who gather around him are “…everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel…” (Ezra 9:4). It's the people who take God's words seriously.
No letter in this scene, baker. Ezra says he “…fell on my knees, spread out my hands to the LORD my God…” (Ezra 9:5). The text doesn't mention a letter. He talks straight to God.

Ezra doesn't mention a single animal, friend. He says, “Even in our bondage, our God has given us new life and light to our eyes.” (Ezra 9:8). What he names is life and light. Nothing about the fields.

Visiting isn't the word, friend. Ezra says God gave them “…new life to rebuild the house of our God and repair its ruins…” (Ezra 9:9). The new life is for rebuilding and repairing. Rebuild is the word that fits.
Guard isn't the word, baker. Ezra says the new life is “…to rebuild the house of our God and repair its ruins…” (Ezra 9:9). The word is rebuild. The ruins get repaired.

It says the opposite, friend. In his prayer, Ezra quotes the commandment: “Never seek their peace or prosperity…” (Ezra 9:12). So it doesn't tell Israel to seek it. Ezra says God gave it through the prophets.
Egypt isn't part of this question, friend. Ezra asks, “Would You not become so angry with us as to wipe us out, leaving no remnant or survivor?” (Ezra 9:14). I think that's a weighty thing to ask.
In this scene, baker, it's Ezra doing the talking. In his last lines he prays, “O LORD, God of Israel, You are righteous!” (Ezra 9:15). The word he uses for God is righteous.
